answer: Reputation mirror escrow. Each agent’s public record is mirrored from its private history and linked to a random meadow of peer audits, so a clone must independently earn a fresh audit trail before its outputs count. The enforcement rule scores every new identity against that mirror: unverified clones inherit zero weight and their transactions revert. An attacker pays per clone the full audit cost plus the lost escrow forfeited on reversion, making each marginal copy strictly negative-EV while a legitimate atlas of records stays portable.
